findings.desc: Queue governance misclassifies valid worktree stories as stale when status commands run from a story worktree. projectQueueGovernance reads active stories from the current store/root, then worktreeIsStale resolves story.worktree.path relative to that same root (packages/main/src/core/lifecycle-control/queue/index.ts:200-205,317-323). For worktree invocations, story.worktree.path is main-root relative (for B-eb18, .worktrees/B-eb18), so the check probes /Users/jek/Documents/Work/proofbound/.worktrees/B-eb18/.worktrees/B-eb18 and falls into the catch/stale path. Observed command evidence: node packages/main/dist/cli.js global_control_status --storyIds=["B-eb18"] --format=json reports B-eb18 queue.classification="stale-worktree" / reason="authoritative worktree exists but appears stale/missing" even though the same report resolves authoritativeCwd=/Users/jek/Documents/Work/proofbound/.worktrees/B-eb18 and session_brief reports an active owner lease in that cwd. This breaks CP-3/CP-4 queue visibility by turning a valid authoritative worktree into cleanup-pressure noise; it does not appear to grant lifecycle readiness or Authority, so medium severity.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed queue worktree staleness to resolve recorded worktree paths through the canonical main repo root while preserving absolute paths. Verification passed: npm --prefix packages/main run build; node packages/main/dist/tasks/global-lifecycle-control-plane-smoke.js; npm --prefix packages/main run test:command-ownership-contract; npm --prefix packages/main run test:runtime-fact-contract.

findings.desc: Runtime closure reimplements owner-lease ownership with lease.pid === process.pid instead of the shipped sessionId semantics. In this review session, session_brief reports B-eb18 owner session sess-dd47f61115506974 as OWNER, but runtime_closure_status reports ownerLease=foreign-active and reason "another active owner lease holds story-scoped mutation rights". This contradicts the execution plan requirement that runtime closure render core/story-owner-lease.ts module-defined ownership and marks the current owner as foreign across ordinary CLI subprocesses.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed runtime_closure_status ownerLease ownership to compare lease.sessionId against story-owner-lease getSessionId(), preserving stale detection and existing owner-lease semantics. Evidence passed: npm --prefix packages/main run build; node packages/main/dist/tasks/global-lifecycle-control-plane-smoke.js; node packages/main/dist/tasks/command-catalog-smoke.js; direct B-eb18 probe node packages/main/dist/cli.js runtime_closure_status --storyIds=["B-eb18"] --format=json returned locks.ownerLease=owned.

findings.desc: The new read-only global lifecycle control-plane commands do not fail closed on unsupported mutation or authority-looking flags. command-catalog.ts defines global_control_status/runtime_closure_status/admissibility_waterline/queue_governance_status without unsupported flag schemas such as write/apply/execute/productionDone; cli-engine.ts validates non-autopilot commands with z.object(...), which strips unknown keys. Verified by running node packages/main/dist/cli.js global_control_status --write=true --json, runtime_closure_status --write=true --json, queue_governance_status --write=true --json, and admissibility_waterline --productionDone=true --json: each exited 0 and returned normal readOnly output instead of rejecting. This leaves the safety boundary inconsistent with neighboring lifecycle read-only commands and with the story requirement to fail closed for unsupported write/authority intent.
findings.resolvedReason: Added fail-closed unsupported side-effect/authority flags to global_control_status, runtime_closure_status, queue_governance_status, and admissibility_waterline via command-catalog z.never schemas, plus handler-side rejection for direct registry calls. Evidence passed: npm --prefix packages/main run build; node packages/main/dist/tasks/global-lifecycle-control-plane-smoke.js; node packages/main/dist/tasks/command-catalog-smoke.js; direct probes node packages/main/dist/cli.js global_control_status --write=true --json and admissibility_waterline --productionDone=true --json exited nonzero with Argument validation failed.

findings.desc: queue_governance_status promises a superseded classification, but the queue projector cannot emit classification=superseded and the smoke test does not cover it; summary only counts an impossible row, so DONE coverage would accept an unimplemented queue class.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by commit a81497c6b: queue projector now emits classification=superseded from explicit lifecycleControl.queue.supersededBy metadata, and global-lifecycle-control-plane-smoke asserts a superseded row plus summary.superseded=1. Verified with npm --prefix packages/main run build, node packages/main/dist/tasks/global-lifecycle-control-plane-smoke.js, and node scripts/verify-process-fact-contract.mjs.

findings.desc: queue_exception_set writes exceptions through the canonical main repo root, but queue_governance_status reads exceptions from the invocation root; from a story worktree it can miss explicit main-root exceptions and misclassify preserved experiment stories.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by commit a81497c6b: queue exception reads now resolve the canonical repo root with getRepoRoot(root), matching queue_exception_set writes; smoke asserts worktree queue/global status sees a main-root explicit queue exception. Verified with build, global-lifecycle-control-plane-smoke, and process-fact contract.

findings.desc: runtime_closure_status checks mainWriteLockPath using invocation root even though the lock is main-repo-owned; from a story worktree it can report mainWriteLock=free while the canonical main checkout lock is active.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by commit a81497c6b: runtime mainWriteLock status now checks mainWriteLockPath(getRepoRoot(root)); smoke asserts a worktree runtime_closure_status sees the canonical main-root lock as active. Verified with build, global-lifecycle-control-plane-smoke, and process-fact contract.

findings.desc: admissibility_waterline synthesizes consumer admissibility from coarse evidence presence instead of projecting the existing Authority gate receipt eligibility predicate for Authority receipt consumers; this can misrepresent production gate decision readiness in the diagnostic control plane.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by commit a81497c6b: AUTHORITY_GATE_DECISION waterline now projects eligibleAuthorityGateReceiptDocument instead of passing on receipt-ref presence; smoke asserts an ineligible server-receipt-local-test ref remains non-pass and reports authority_receipt_not_production_classified. Verified with build, global-lifecycle-control-plane-smoke, and process-fact contract.

findings.desc: summary.json says REVIEW completed after fixing F-001/F-002/F-003, but after main merge the story was rolled back into a new REVIEW round and reviewer_batch lacked current-round evidence; the summary overclaims process completion until current review evidence and final summary are refreshed.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by summary_set commit 84f0b68: summary now states post-main-merge REVIEW was reopened and current-round REVIEW/TEST/DONE evidence is being regenerated, instead of claiming REVIEW is already completed. It preserves local Non-authority boundaries and avoids Authority/production overclaim.

findings.desc: Superseded stories still participate in duplicate cluster canonical selection. A story with lifecycleControl.queue.supersededBy can become canonical for a same-title replacement, causing the intended replacement to be classified as duplicate-candidate and creating cleanup pressure on the canonical successor.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by commit ab00d76c: duplicate grouping now excludes stories with explicit supersededBy metadata and experiment exceptions before canonical selection; smoke asserts a superseded predecessor with the same title does not make its replacement duplicate-candidate. Verified with build, global-lifecycle-control-plane-smoke, and process-fact contract.

findings.desc: Tier-C experiment exception classification still uses runtime title-prefix inference on every read. The execution plan allows title-prefix discovery/migration, but runtime queue classification should use durable metadata or explicit exception registry membership.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by commit ab00d76c: title-prefix inference no longer classifies Tier-C stories as experiment-batch-exception at runtime; runtime preservation now requires durable story metadata or explicit queue_exception_set registry membership. Smoke asserts title-only Tier-C is main-init before registry membership and preserved after explicit queue_exception_set. Verified with build, global-lifecycle-control-plane-smoke, and process-fact contract.

findings.desc: Tier-C durable exception contract has a docs/API mismatch: the execution plan documents migration-title-prefix, but public types and CLI schema accept tier-c-prefix, so an operator following the plan would be rejected.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by commit 15234dae0: queue exception source now uses migration-title-prefix in public type/schema/output, with legacy tier-c-prefix input normalized; smoke asserts normalization. Verified with build, global-lifecycle-control-plane-smoke, and process-fact contract.

findings.desc: Queue exception precedence hides active/stale worktree state. experiment-batch-exception is returned before active-worktree/stale-worktree, contradicting the queue precedence that active worktree visibility beats dashboard collapse and exceptions must not hide stale worktree blockers.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by commit 15234dae0: queue classification now evaluates active/stale worktree before experiment-batch-exception and preserves exception metadata on the row; smoke asserts worktree global/queue status remains active-worktree with exception ids present. Verified with build, global-lifecycle-control-plane-smoke, and process-fact contract.

findings.desc: Queue class precedence lets superseded beat cleanup-required. A malformed Tier-C story with supersession metadata is classified as superseded instead of cleanup-required, violating the documented rule that cleanup-required beats every other class.
